key_insight: Stepped target-bias control turns self-limiting electrospray deposition into a multilayer process, enabling thickness to increase layer-by-layer instead of being fixed by one spray pass.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to conformal, bias-tunable coatings on complex 3D surfaces, bridging electrospray deposition with nanoscale-to-microscale film design for advanced coatings and composites.
method: Apply electrospray deposition in the self-limiting regime.
Use a secondary target bias to reduce and tune deposited thickness.
Remove bias stepwise to build tri-layer and multilayer stacks; combine with capillary rise infiltration for robust nanocomposites.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports tri-layer polystyrene stacks with bias-controlled thickness, uniform tri-layer coatings on complex geometry, and mechanically robust nanocomposites after CaRI infiltration.
watch_item: Thickness and uniformity depend on precise voltage stepping and spray/material parameters, so reproducibility and process control may be sensitive to setup calibration.
paper_title: Multilayer Self‐Limiting Electrospray Deposition via Stepped Voltage Bias
